claims.claim: Justin Martyr was an early Christian apologist and philosopher, born c. 100 at Flavia Neapolis in Palestine and martyred c. 165 in Rome.
The Second Apology was written as a supplement to Justin's First Apology, between 150 and 157 CE.
The work was occasioned by proceedings that had taken place in Rome under Lollius Urbicus as prefect of the city, specifically the condemnation of Christians to death.
The Second Apology is addressed to the Roman Senate.
The work recounts the case of a Christian woman who divorced her immoral husband, who then retaliated by accusing her and subsequently Christian leaders before the authorities.
The Second Apology survived in a single Greek manuscript of the year 1364, together with the First Apology and the Dialogue with Trypho.
Justin argues that fallen angels and demons incite hatred against Christians, and that these demons are the spirits of offspring born through union of fallen angels and women before the Flood.
Justin points to the fearlessness of Christians in the face of death as proof that they are not pleasure-seekers and therefore could not be guilty of the crimes alleged against them.
